title: Typography as Meaning — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Typography as Meaning's rich face, its first round, a Study and still a proposal. Two made walks test the page's grammar: one reads it blind, one part at a time, and asks the reader before any label shows; the other puts all 120 answer-sets through the page's own lettering function and runs it backwards, to count what the form can give back. Beside them sit the page's two proofs and BLUELINE's renders, gathered as they were. I grow when the page is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: Counted on whos-talking.html's own letter() over all 120 answer-sets: 95 forms to a ruler, 80 to the eye (only the margin's 2 px shift merged), 73 if the small type steps (21 against 24 px, 16.8 against 19.2) are merged too, 58 if size isn't read; numbers confirmed by the challenger. Inside or outside reads back 120/120; to whom 80/120. The page's sentence is right where source and feeling want the same channel, but precedence is set per source as well as per channel: a radio takes the balloon and the face and leaves the feeling only size and case, so a menacing radio is a calm one 6 px larger (24 → 30); a mind takes the balloon and the case; the narrator takes everything but a tremor; outside the story the margin takes the balloon from every voice but the narrator's. Sharper: the to-whom loss comes from the grammar using the margin for two things, 'outside the story' (Placement) and 'addresses us' (Tail), so a voice already outside has no mark left for 'to us' but 2 px. A possible line: 'Run as a function, the precedence is set per source: a radio takes the balloon and the face and leaves the feeling only its size, so a menacing radio is a calm one 6 px larger; a mind takes the balloon and the case; the narrator takes everything but a tremor. And the margin does two jobs, outside the story and to us, so a voice already outside cannot turn to us.'

Beside 'the balloon as authored geometry', an observation, not a claim: BLUELINE's canny sweep lost the guide's thin tail at both strengths tried (0.35, 0.5; one guide, one seed, one word), and its gen-AI montage draws every tail with balloon_lib after the render, so the model never touches them. A possible clause: 'BLUELINE's canny sweep lost the guide's tail at both strengths tried; its montage draws the tails after the render.' The test that would earn more: tail survival at cn 0.65, 0.8 and 1.0, thin and filled, in BLUELINE's queued sweep.

pieces.file: Typography as Meaning — rich — the grammar, blind.html
pieces.title: the grammar, blind · a walk in four steps
pieces.caption: **Read the grammar before the labels.** One part changes at a time, and you order or name the forms before the key shows: weight (quiet to loud), case (private to public), hand or type (the author or someone in the story), and last the balloon's outline alone, with no tail and the same words in all seven. Then the tally against chance. One reader is a sign, not a measurement.

verdicts.file: Typography as Meaning — rich — the grammar, blind.html
verdicts.why: A test: the reader can fall to chance and the verdict says so; chance levels exact (n(n−1)/4 pairs, 1 in n!; 1 of 7 named), key locked until every answer is given, shuffles leak no order. Note: start-over after the key lets a reader retry unmarked.

pieces.caption: **Is the form really chosen by the four answers, and can you read them back?** One balloon, then one answer changed at a time, then a menacing radio under either order of precedence, and last all 120 answer-sets put through the page's own function (whos-talking.html's `letter()`, copied unchanged) and counted: 95 forms to a ruler, 80 to the eye, 58 if size isn't read.
pieces.near: That is what makes lettering a language rather than decoration
